title: UX Value, Product Risk, and What Not to Digitise

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Last time, evidence changed CarePath's plan. Now the team has three new proposals: mandatory digital booking, automatic symptom triage, and no phone support after launch.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: That sounds efficient on a roadmap. Today we're asking whether any of it creates real value, and for whom?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Exactly. Start with the phone line. What happens if it disappears?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Straightforward requests may move faster. But someone in crisis, or without reliable access, loses the help that makes the task possible.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: So whose cost did the saving remove?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: It may have shifted work to patients and hidden failures from the product dashboard. Staff could still spend more time handling exceptions elsewhere.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: How would you assess the automatic triage idea?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: The possible error is serious. A confident wrong answer could delay care. We'd need clinical evidence, oversight, a clear boundary on what it may do, and recourse.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Could technology help without taking that authority?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Yes. Show service criteria, broad availability, preparation, and referral status. Assist staff with structured matching, but keep unusual cases and clinical urgency with accountable people.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Let people understand the service before asking them to register. Require identity when it's actually needed to submit or manage a request.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Notice the choice isn't ‘build it’ or ‘do nothing.’

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: We could repair information, support human work, automate one bounded step, or change the service rule itself.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Which risk would you investigate first?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: The one with high consequence and weak evidence. Not the harmless preference that's easiest to test.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Good. What does the first release do?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Improve discovery, referral visibility, preparation, and reuse of information. Keep phone support connected to the same status. Treat symptom triage as a research question, not a promise.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: That's the end of our foundation: use digital tools where they make a worthwhile outcome more reachable, and keep human judgment where it protects that outcome.
